question: What was Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier's most important contribution to chemistry in 1789?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Law of Conservation of Mass.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier, often called the 'Father of Modern Chemistry', formulated the Law of Conservation of Mass in his 1789 work *Traité Élémentaire de Chimie* (Elementary Treatise on Chemistry). (द्रव्यमान संरक्षण का नियम — लेवोज़िए)

 

• The law states that mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction — the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.

 

• Lavoisier established this through careful quantitative experiments involving combustion, showing that mass is conserved even though matter changes form.

 

• He also disproved the phlogiston theory, correctly explained combustion as a reaction with oxygen, and helped devise the modern system of chemical nomenclature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lavoisier is also credited with naming oxygen and hydrogen, and co-authoring *Méthode de Nomenclature Chimique* (1787), which laid the foundation for modern chemical naming.

 

• He was executed during the French Revolution in 1794.

 

NOTE

 

• Law of Multiple Proportions (Option 2): Proposed by John Dalton in 1803; it deals with elements combining in different ratios to form different compounds.

 

• Law of Definite Proportions (Option 3): Proposed by Joseph Proust; it states a compound always contains its constituent elements in a fixed ratio by mass.

 

• Law of Conservation of Energy (Option 4): A distinct physical law stating energy can neither be created nor destroyed; not the specific contribution attributed to Lavoisier in 1789.

question: An electric iron requires a ________ fuse to prevent short circuiting.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5 A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An electric iron is a high-wattage appliance (typically 750-1000 W), and standard household wiring practice prescribes a 5 A fuse/plug for such appliances to safely carry the load without blowing under normal operation. (फ्यूज़ — इलेक्ट्रिक आयरन के लिए 5 एम्पियर)

 

• A fuse is a safety device containing a thin wire that melts and breaks the circuit when current exceeds a safe limit, protecting the appliance and wiring from damage due to short circuits or overloads.

 

• Lower-wattage appliances like bulbs, fans and radios typically use a 3 A fuse, while higher-wattage appliances like irons, heaters and geysers use a 5 A (or higher) fuse.

 

• The fuse rating is chosen to be slightly above the appliance's normal operating current but well below the level that would damage the wiring.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fuse wire is typically made of a low-melting-point alloy of tin and lead.

 

• In modern installations, Miniature Circuit Breakers (MCBs) are increasingly used in place of traditional fuses for the same protective function.

 

NOTE

 

• 4 A (Option 1): Not the standard rating used for high-wattage appliances such as irons.

 

• 3 A (Option 2): This rating is used for low-wattage appliances like table lamps and fans, not for an iron.

 

• 2 A (Option 3): Too low a rating for the current drawn by a high-wattage electric iron; it would blow under normal use.

question: Who among the following is primarily connected to the World's Parliament of Religions convened in Chicago, 1893?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swami Vivekananda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Swami Vivekananda represented Hinduism and India at the World's Parliament of Religions, held in Chicago, USA, in September 1893. (विश्व धर्म संसद, शिकागो — स्वामी विवेकानंद)

 

• His opening address, beginning with "Sisters and Brothers of America", received a standing ovation and introduced Vedanta and Hindu philosophy to a global audience.

 

• He was a chief disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahansa and founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897, dedicated to service (seva) and spiritual practice.

 

• His visit to the USA is commemorated in India as National Youth Day (12 January), his birthday.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vivekananda's real name was Narendranath Datta; he took the monastic name Vivekananda before travelling to the USA.

 

• The World's Parliament of Religions 1893 was part of the World's Columbian Exposition and is considered the birth of the modern interfaith movement.

 

NOTE

 

• Dayanand Saraswati (Option 1): Founder of the Arya Samaj (1875); he died in 1883, a decade before the 1893 Parliament, and was not associated with it.

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy (Option 3): Founder of the Brahmo Samaj; a 19th-century social reformer who died in 1833, long before the event.

 

• Ramakrishna Paramhansa (Option 4): Vivekananda's spiritual guru; he died in 1886 and did not himself attend the Chicago Parliament.

question: Khuallam is a famous dance of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mizoram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Khuallam, meaning the 'dance of the guests', is a traditional folk dance of Mizoram, performed to welcome guests, typically on festive occasions such as Chapchar Kut. (खुआल्लम नृत्य — मिजोरम)

 

• It is usually performed by men wearing traditional attire such as Puanchei and ornamental headgear, to the beat of drums (khuang) and gongs.

 

• The dance reflects the hospitality and community spirit central to Mizo culture.

 

• Mizoram's other popular folk dances include Cheraw (Bamboo dance), Chheihlam, and Solakia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chapchar Kut is the most important and colourful festival of Mizoram, celebrated in spring after jhum (shifting) cultivation clearing.

 

• Cheraw, the bamboo dance of Mizoram, is one of the oldest and most iconic dances of the state, performed using pairs of bamboo staves.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar (Option 1): Known for folk dances like Jat-Jatin and Jhijhian, not Khuallam.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 2): Known for dances such as Kuchipudi and Dappu, not Khuallam.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 4): Known for dances such as Kathak and Raslila, not Khuallam.

question: The concept of Public Interest Litigation originated in _______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is USA.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The concept of Public Interest Litigation (PIL) originated in the United States of America during the 1960s-70s, as a legal tool to give access to justice for disadvantaged and marginalised groups. (जनहित याचिका — संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका में उत्पत्ति)

 

• In India, PIL was pioneered in the late 1970s and early 1980s by Justices P.N. Bhagwati and V.R. Krishna Iyer, who relaxed the traditional rule of *locus standi* to allow any public-spirited citizen to approach the courts on behalf of those unable to do so themselves.

 

• PIL enables courts to be approached under Article 32 (Supreme Court) and Article 226 (High Courts) of the Constitution for enforcement of the fundamental rights of the public at large.

 

• Landmark early Indian PIL cases include Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar (1979), concerning undertrial prisoners.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• PIL is also referred to as Social Action Litigation (SAL) in the Indian context.

 

• It has been used in India to address issues ranging from environmental protection to bonded labour and prison reforms.

 

NOTE

 

• Switzerland (Option 1): Not the country of origin of the PIL concept.

 

• Iceland (Option 2): Not associated with the origin of PIL.

 

• New Zealand (Option 4): Not associated with the origin of PIL.

question: Thrissur Pooram is one of the famous temple festivals celebrated in _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thrissur Pooram is one of the most famous and spectacular temple festivals of Kerala, held annually at the Vadakkunnathan Temple, Thrissur. (त्रिशूर पूरम — केरल)

 

• It was instituted by Sakthan Thampuran, the Maharaja of Cochin, in the late 18th century, bringing together various temples of the region for a grand celebration.

 

• The festival is famous for its spectacular parade of caparisoned elephants, elaborate 'kudamattam' (umbrella-changing) display, and traditional percussion ensembles like Panchari Melam and Pandi Melam, followed by fireworks.

 

• It is celebrated in the Malayalam month of Medam (April-May).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala's other major temple festivals include Attukal Pongala and the Aranmula Boat Race.

 

• Thrissur is popularly known as the 'Cultural Capital of Kerala'.

 

NOTE

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 1): Not the location of Thrissur Pooram.

 

• Karnataka (Option 3): Not the location of Thrissur Pooram.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 4): Not the location of Thrissur Pooram.

question: Identify the group of districts that are NOT an example of industrial districts of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alwar and Bhiwani.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alwar (Rajasthan) and Bhiwani (Haryana) are not conventionally classed among India's well-known industrial-cluster district pairs; they are primarily agrarian districts with only localised, small-scale industrial activity. (औद्योगिक जिले — अलवर और भिवानी अपवाद)

 

• In contrast, Kanpur and Agra are historically important for the leather industry, Jabalpur and Bhopal are notable for ordnance/engineering industries, and Cuttack and Kota have their own established industrial and manufacturing activity.

 

• Such district-pair groupings are commonly used in SSC-level geography questions to test familiarity with India's traditional industrial belts and clusters.

 

• India's industrial districts are generally identified by the presence of large-scale, long-established manufacturing activity, access to raw materials, transport links and skilled labour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's major industrial regions include the Mumbai-Pune region, the Hooghly region, the Bangalore-Chennai region and the Gujarat region, among others.

 

• District-level industrial clusters often develop around a specific traditional craft or product, such as leather (Kanpur, Agra) or brassware (Moradabad).

 

NOTE

 

• Cuttack and Kota (Option 1): Both are established centres of industrial/manufacturing activity, so this pair does not fit the 'NOT an example' criterion.

 

• Kanpur and Agra (Option 2): Both are well-known for the leather industry and are recognised industrial districts.

 

• Jabalpur and Bhopal (Option 4): Both host significant engineering and ordnance-related industries and are recognised industrial districts.

question:
Match the concepts in column A with their respective descriptions in column B.

Column A: a. Gross national product, b. Net national product, c. Personal income, d. Disposable personal income

Column B: 1. Annual income received by the individual's production in a given period, 2. After the tax of personal income, 3. Money value of the national output, 4. Net production of goods services during the year
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-3, b-4, c-1, d-2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gross National Product (a) is the money value of the national output (3) — the total market value of all final goods and services produced by a country's nationals, within and outside the country, in a year. (सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद — राष्ट्रीय उत्पादन का मौद्रिक मूल्य)

 

• Net National Product (b) equals the net production of goods and services during the year (4) — i.e., GNP minus depreciation (consumption of fixed capital).

 

• Personal Income (c) is the annual income received by individuals from their production/factor contributions in a given period (1) — it includes transfer payments and excludes undistributed profits and corporate taxes.

 

• Disposable Personal Income (d) is what remains after the tax on personal income (2) — i.e., Personal Income minus direct personal taxes, available for consumption and saving.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• NNP = GNP − Depreciation, and National Income (NI) = NNP at factor cost.

 

• Disposable Personal Income = Personal Income − Personal Taxes, and is the actual amount households can spend or save.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (a-2, b-1, c-3, d-4): Incorrectly swaps the definitions of GNP and Personal Income with NNP and Disposable Income.

 

• Option 2 (a-3, b-1, c-2, d-4): Correctly matches GNP (a-3), but wrongly matches NNP, Personal Income and Disposable Income.

 

• Option 4 (a-4, b-3, c-2, d-1): Reverses the correct matches for GNP/NNP and Personal Income/Disposable Income.

question: Ustad Zia Mohiuddin Dagar was a ___________ player of profound depth, favouring sparse and slow realisations of ragas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rudra veena.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Zia Mohiuddin Dagar was a renowned Rudra Veena player belonging to the Dagar family, custodians of the Dhrupad style of Hindustani classical music. (रुद्र वीणा — जिया मोहिउद्दीन डागर)

 

• He was celebrated for his deep, meditative and slow *alap*-based renditions of ragas, staying true to the austere, unhurried aesthetic of the Dhrupad-Been tradition.

 

• He significantly redesigned the Rudra Veena to improve its sustain and tonal depth, and trained several notable disciples, including his son Bahauddin Dagar.

 

• The Dagar family is one of the oldest lineages of Dhrupad vocalists and instrumentalists in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rudra Veena is a large stick zither with two gourd resonators, considered one of the oldest and most revered instruments of Hindustani classical music.

 

• Dhrupad is the oldest surviving form of Hindustani classical vocal music, characterised by its serious, meditative style.

 

NOTE

 

• Sitar (Option 1): A plucked string instrument popularised by artists like Ravi Shankar and Vilayat Khan, distinct from the Rudra Veena.

 

• Violin (Option 2): A bowed instrument; not associated with Zia Mohiuddin Dagar.

 

• Flute (Option 3): Associated with artists like Hariprasad Chaurasia, not Zia Mohiuddin Dagar.

question: The headquarters of the second Green Revolution cell was in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Patna.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The headquarters of the Second Green Revolution cell, aimed at bringing a green revolution to Eastern India, was established at Patna, Bihar. (द्वितीय हरित क्रांति प्रकोष्ठ — पटना)

 

• The initiative aimed to raise agricultural productivity in the eastern states — Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Assam and eastern Uttar Pradesh — which have abundant water resources but lagged behind the traditional Green Revolution states of Punjab and Haryana.

 

• ICAR's Research Complex for Eastern Region (ICAR-RCER), Patna, was closely associated with coordinating this eastern green revolution effort.

 

• The scheme focuses on improving rice-based cropping systems, irrigation, and extension services across the eastern Indo-Gangetic plains.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI) programme was launched as a sub-scheme under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) in 2010-11.

 

• The original Green Revolution of the 1960s-70s was primarily concentrated in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Raipur (Option 1): Not the headquarters of the second Green Revolution cell.

 

• Kolkata (Option 3): Not the headquarters of the second Green Revolution cell.

 

• Bhubaneswar (Option 4): Not the headquarters of the second Green Revolution cell.

question: Who was the Viceroy of India when Mahatma Gandhi started Dandi March on 12 March 1930?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Irwin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Irwin (Viceroy of India, 1926-1931) was the Viceroy when Mahatma Gandhi launched the Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha) on 12 March 1930, walking from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi in Gujarat to break the salt law. (डांडी मार्च — लॉर्ड इरविन)

 

• The march covered about 240 miles (390 km) over 24 days, culminating on 6 April 1930, when Gandhi broke the salt law by making salt from seawater.

 

• Lord Irwin later negotiated the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931), under which civil disobedience was suspended and Gandhi agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference.

 

• The Dandi March marked the beginning of the Civil Disobedience Movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lord Irwin later became known as Lord Halifax and played a prominent role in British politics before World War II.

 

• The First Round Table Conference (1930) was held without Congress participation, largely because of the ongoing Civil Disobedience Movement.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Chelmsford (Option 1): Viceroy from 1916-1921; associated with the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919) and the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, not the Dandi March.

 

• Lord Minto II (Option 2): Viceroy from 1905-1910; associated with the Morley-Minto Reforms (1909), not the Dandi March.

 

• Lord Willingdon (Option 4): Viceroy from 1931-1936; became Viceroy only after the Dandi March had already taken place.

question: Who is the world's most popular leader as per Global Leader Approval Ratings released by US-based Morning Consult in February 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narendra Modi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Global Leader Approval Ratings released by the US-based Morning Consult in February 2023, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi topped the list as the world's most popular leader, with an approval rating of around 78%. (सर्वाधिक लोकप्रिय वैश्विक नेता — नरेंद्र मोदी)

 

• Morning Consult is a US-based technology and media company that conducts regular surveys tracking the approval ratings of heads of government/state across multiple countries.

 

• Modi has consistently topped or featured near the top of these rankings in subsequent surveys as well, ahead of leaders such as Mexico's AMLO and other G20 heads of government.

 

• Leaders such as Joe Biden (USA) and Vladimir Putin (Russia) featured lower down the list in the same survey.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Morning Consult's approval trackers are based on daily online surveys of adults in each country and are widely cited in international media as an indicator of political standing.

 

• PM Modi remained at or near the top of these global leader approval rankings through much of 2023 and 2024.

 

NOTE

 

• Xi Jinping (Option 1): President of China; ranked lower in this particular Morning Consult survey.

 

• Vladimir Putin (Option 2): President of Russia; ranked lower in this particular Morning Consult survey.

 

• Joe Biden (Option 3): President of the USA; ranked lower in this particular Morning Consult survey.

question: In which year was Smart Cities Mission launched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2015.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Smart Cities Mission was launched by the Government of India on 25 June 2015, along with the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) and the Housing for All (PMAY-Urban) mission. (स्मार्ट सिटी मिशन — 25 जून 2015)

 

• The mission aims to promote cities that provide core infrastructure, a clean and sustainable environment, and a good quality of life through 'smart' solutions, using area-based development and pan-city initiatives.

 

• Cities were selected through a City Challenge/competition method, based on criteria like existing service levels, institutional systems and citizen engagement.

 

• The mission initially covered 100 cities, selected across multiple rounds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Smart Cities Mission is administered by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

 

• Key components include Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) set up at the city level to plan, implement and manage the mission.

 

NOTE

 

• 2013 (Option 2): No such mission was launched in this year.

 

• 2019 (Option 3): Incorrect year; the mission had already been operational for several years by 2019.

 

• 2018 (Option 4): Incorrect year; the mission was launched earlier, in 2015.

question: Which of the following nations won the seven times women's Asia Cup cricket Championship?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian women's cricket team is the most successful side in the Women's Asia Cup, having won the title seven times — in 2004, 2005-06, 2006, 2008, 2012, 2016 and 2022. (महिला एशिया कप — भारत, सात बार विजेता)

 

• The tournament, organised by the Asian Cricket Council (ACC), has been held in both ODI and T20I formats over the years, with India dominating most editions since its inception in 2004.

 

• India's title in 2022 (held in Bangladesh) came under the captaincy of Harmanpreet Kaur.

 

• Sri Lanka ended India's dominance by winning the 2024 edition, but that does not change India's tally of seven titles referred to in the question.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bangladesh won the 2018 Women's Asia Cup, the only edition between 2004 and 2022 that India did not win.

 

• The Women's Asia Cup has been contested in T20I format since 2012.

 

NOTE

 

• Pakistan (Option 1): Has never won the Women's Asia Cup title.

 

• Bangladesh (Option 2): Won the tournament once, in 2018, not seven times.

 

• Sri Lanka (Option 4): Won the 2024 edition but has not won the title seven times.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides that the State must secure a social order to promote the welfare of people?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 38.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 38 of the Indian Constitution, part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), directs the State to secure a social order for the promotion of the welfare of the people by minimising inequalities in income, status, facilities and opportunities. (अनुच्छेद 38 — कल्याणकारी सामाजिक व्यवस्था)

 

• Article 38(1) mandates the State to strive to promote the welfare of the people by securing and protecting a social order in which justice — social, economic and political — informs all institutions of national life.

 

• Article 38(2), added by the 44th Constitutional Amendment (1978), specifically directs the State to minimise inequalities in income and to endeavour to eliminate inequalities in status, facilities and opportunities.

 

• DPSPs, laid down in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Constitution, are non-justiciable but fundamental in the governance of the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 39 lays down certain principles of policy to be followed by the State, such as equal pay for equal work and adequate means of livelihood.

 

• DPSPs are inspired by the Irish Constitution and are described as 'instruments of instructions' to the government.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 37 (Option 1): States that DPSPs are not enforceable by courts but are fundamental in governance; it does not itself lay down the specific 'social order' welfare directive.

 

• Article 39 (Option 3): Lays down specific principles of policy (e.g., equitable distribution of resources), distinct from the general welfare mandate of Article 38.

 

• Article 36 (Option 4): Merely defines the term 'State' for the purposes of Part IV.

question: Identify a water-harvesting system found in Jaisalmer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khadins.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Khadins are a traditional rainwater/floodwater harvesting system found in the Jaisalmer district of Rajasthan, used to capture surface runoff for agriculture in the arid Thar Desert region. (खडीन — जैसलमेर की जल संग्रहण प्रणाली)

 

• A Khadin consists of a long earthen embankment (bund) built across the lower hill slopes to impound rainwater, allowing silt and moisture to accumulate for crop cultivation once the water recedes.

 

• This technique, developed by the Paliwal Brahmins of Jaisalmer around the 15th century, is similar in principle to the eri/tank systems of South India.

 

• Khadin farming is especially suited to growing crops like gram, wheat and other rabi crops in a region with very low rainfall.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other traditional Rajasthani water-harvesting structures include Kunds/Tankas (underground water storage tanks) and Nadis (village ponds).

 

• Rajasthan's traditional water-harvesting systems are often cited as models of sustainable water management in arid zones.

 

NOTE

 

• Guls (Option 1): Diversion channels/watercourses used in the hilly regions of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh to carry water from mountain streams.

 

• Johads (Option 2): Small earthen check dams/village ponds used for water harvesting in Alwar and other parts of Rajasthan, not specifically Jaisalmer.

 

• Kuls (Option 4): Traditional irrigation channels found in the mountainous regions of Himachal Pradesh, not Jaisalmer.

question: The _________ were tributary chiefs of the Gupta dynasty. They established an independent kingdom in western India. Dhruvasena II was the most important ruler of this kingdom.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maitrakas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Maitrakas were originally tributary chiefs (military governors) under the Gupta Empire who established an independent kingdom in western India, with their capital at Vallabhi (in present-day Gujarat), after the decline of Gupta power. (मैत्रक वंश — वल्लभी, गुजरात)

 

• Dhruvasena II, who married a Chalukya princess and is referred to in the accounts of the Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang), was one of the most important rulers of this dynasty.

 

• Vallabhi, their capital, developed into a major centre of learning, particularly for Buddhist education, rivalling Nalanda.

 

• The Maitraka dynasty ruled from around the 5th to 8th century CE, until it was eventually overrun by Arab invasions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhattarka is traditionally regarded as the founder of the Maitraka dynasty.

 

• Vallabhi University, associated with the Maitrakas, was a renowned centre of Buddhist learning in ancient India.

 

NOTE

 

• Maukharis (Option 2): A dynasty that ruled in the region around Kannauj in north India, not tributary chiefs of the Guptas in western India.

 

• Pushyabhutis (Option 3): The dynasty of Harshavardhana, ruling from Thanesar/Kannauj, unrelated to the Gupta tributary chiefs of western India.

 

• Gurjara Pratiharas (Option 4): A later dynasty (8th-11th century CE) that ruled over parts of northern and western India, distinct from the Gupta-era Maitrakas.

question: As of 31 May 2021, only 47% of total routes and 39% of airports (unserved and underserved) have been operationalised under UDAN, according to ICRA. What is the full form of UDAN?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ude Desh Ka Aam Naagrik.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• UDAN stands for "Ude Desh Ka Aam Naagrik" (Let the common citizen of the country fly), a regional connectivity scheme of the Government of India launched under the National Civil Aviation Policy (2016). (उड़ान योजना — उड़े देश का आम नागरिक)

 

• UDAN aims to make air travel affordable for the common man by connecting unserved and underserved airports/airstrips, with airlines receiving Viability Gap Funding (VGF) to keep fares low on identified routes.

 

• The scheme was launched by the Ministry of Civil Aviation in 2016, with the first UDAN flight taking off in April 2017.

 

• The question refers to a May 2021 ICRA assessment, which noted that only about 47% of routes and 39% of airports sanctioned under UDAN had actually been operationalised by that date.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• UDAN also includes special variants such as UDAN-International and support for heliports and seaplanes to improve regional and remote connectivity.

 

• The scheme is implemented through a bidding process where airlines propose routes under different Route Dispersal Guidelines (RDG) categories.

 

NOTE

 

• Udtha Desh Ka Aam Nayak (Option 1): Not the correct expansion of UDAN; this phrasing does not correspond to the official scheme name.

 

• Unnath Desh Ka Aam Naagrik (Option 3): Not the correct expansion of UDAN.

 

• Ujwal Desh Ka Aam Naagrik (Option 4): Not the correct expansion of UDAN.

question: Which of the following options is the most appropriate cause for unemployment in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Over population.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Over-population is widely regarded as one of the most significant and direct causes of unemployment in India, as the rapid growth of the labour force outpaces the economy's capacity to generate adequate job opportunities. (जनसंख्या वृद्धि — बेरोजगारी का प्रमुख कारण)

 

• India's high population growth rate has historically resulted in a labour surplus, particularly in rural and agricultural sectors, leading to disguised and seasonal unemployment.

 

• Rapid population growth also puts pressure on capital formation and infrastructure, making it harder for job creation to keep pace with the number of new entrants to the workforce each year.

 

• Other structural causes of unemployment in India include slow industrial growth, the seasonal nature of agriculture, and a skills mismatch with market demand.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's unemployment is often categorised into types such as disguised unemployment, seasonal unemployment, structural unemployment and educated unemployment.

 

• Government programmes like MGNREGA aim to address rural unemployment by guaranteeing wage employment.

 

NOTE

 

• Environment conditions (Option 2): Not identified as a primary or direct cause of unemployment in India.

 

• High educational systems (Option 3): A well-developed educational system is not, by itself, a cause of unemployment (though a mismatch between education and market needs can contribute to 'educated unemployment').

 

• Lack of labour force (Option 4): India has a labour surplus, not a shortage, so this is not a recognised cause of unemployment.

question: As of the June 2021, how many biosphere reserves are established in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 18.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As of June 2021, India had 18 Biosphere Reserves, designated by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change to conserve representative ecosystems along with their flora, fauna and the traditional lifestyle of the area. (जैवमंडल निचय — भारत में 18)

 

• Biosphere Reserves are notified under the Man and Biosphere (MAB) Programme of UNESCO, though not all national biosphere reserves are internationally recognised by UNESCO.

 

• The first Biosphere Reserve in India, the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, was established in 1986.

 

• Several of India's biosphere reserves — such as Nilgiri, Nanda Devi, Gulf of Mannar, Sundarbans, Nokrek, Pachmarhi, Similipal, Achanakmar-Amarkantak, Great Nicobar, Agasthyamalai, Khangchendzonga and Panna — are included in the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Biosphere Reserves are typically organised into a core zone, a buffer zone and a transition/manipulation zone.

 

• Additional biosphere reserves have since been designated, but the question specifically asks about the number as of June 2021.

 

NOTE

 

• 20 (Option 2): Not the count as of June 2021.

 

• 26 (Option 3): Not the count as of June 2021; overstates the number.

 

• 15 (Option 4): Understates the number of biosphere reserves as of June 2021.

question: In which of the following battles did Muhammad of Ghor defeat Jayachandra of Gahadavala dynasty in 1194 AD?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Battle of Chandawar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Battle of Chandawar (1194 CE), fought near the Yamuna river in present-day Uttar Pradesh, saw Muhammad of Ghor (Muhammad Ghori) defeat Jayachandra, the Gahadavala (Gahadwal) ruler of Kannauj. (चंदावर का युद्ध — मुहम्मद गौरी बनाम जयचंद)

 

• Jayachandra was killed in the battle, and his defeat marked the end of the powerful Gahadavala kingdom and opened the Gangetic plains to Ghurid conquest.

 

• This victory, following closely after the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 CE) against Prithviraj Chauhan, consolidated Ghurid control over northern India and paved the way for the establishment of the Delhi Sultanate.

 

• Muhammad Ghori's slave general Qutb-ud-din Aibak later became the first ruler of the Delhi Sultanate (Mamluk/Slave dynasty).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Gahadavala dynasty ruled the Kannauj region and was known for its patronage of Sanskrit learning.

 

• The years 1192 and 1194 together mark the decisive Ghurid conquests over the Chauhans and the Gahadavalas, respectively, which effectively ended Rajput dominance in north India.

 

NOTE

 

• First battle of Tarain (Option 1): Fought in 1191, in which Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori, not Jayachandra.

 

• Battle of Anhilwara (Option 3): An early, unsuccessful expedition (1178) by Muhammad Ghori against the Solanki (Chalukya) ruler of Gujarat, not related to Jayachandra.

 

• Second battle of Tarain (Option 4): Fought in 1192, in which Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan, not Jayachandra.

question: The growth form of a plant, comprising its size, shape and orientation is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is habit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In botany, the 'habit' of a plant refers to its general growth form — comprising its overall size, shape, orientation (erect, climbing, prostrate, etc.) and branching pattern. (वृद्धि रूप — 'हैबिट')

 

• Plant habit is commonly classified into categories such as herb, shrub, tree, climber and creeper, based on features like stem type, height and lignification.

 

• Habit is distinct from habitat, which refers to the natural environment/place where an organism lives.

 

• Describing plant habit is one of the first steps in plant morphology and taxonomic description.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common plant habits recognised in taxonomy include annual, biennial and perennial herbs, shrubs, trees, lianas (woody climbers) and succulents.

 

• Plant habit is an important diagnostic character used in field identification and classification of plants.

 

NOTE

 

• Environment (Option 2): Refers to the surrounding physical, chemical and biological conditions affecting an organism, not its growth form.

 

• Habitat (Option 3): Refers to the natural place/environment where an organism normally lives, distinct from its growth form.

 

• Growth pattern (Option 4): Not the standard botanical term for this concept; 'habit' is the precise term used.

question: When and where did India win its first World Championships medal in Athletics?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2003, France.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won its first-ever medal at the World Championships in Athletics when Anju Bobby George claimed the bronze medal in the women's long jump at the 2003 World Championships in Athletics, held in Paris/Saint-Denis, France. (एथलेटिक्स विश्व चैंपियनशिप 2003 — अंजू बॉबी जॉर्ज, फ्रांस)

 

• Her jump of 6.70 metres secured the bronze, making her the first Indian to win a medal at the World Athletics Championships.

 

• Anju Bobby George also won a bronze at the 2005 IAAF World Athletics Final and was ranked among the world's top long jumpers in the mid-2000s.

 

• She was awarded the Padma Shri (2004) and earlier the Arjuna Award (2002) for her achievements.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The World Athletics Championships are held once every two years, organised by World Athletics (formerly IAAF).

 

• India's other notable World Athletics Championships medal is Neeraj Chopra's gold in the javelin throw at the 2023 World Championships in Budapest.

 

NOTE

 

• 2009, Germany (Option 1): The 2009 World Championships were held in Berlin, Germany, but this was not India's first medal at the event.

 

• 2005, Finland (Option 2): The 2005 World Championships were held in Helsinki, Finland; India's first medal had already come in 2003.

 

• 2007, Japan (Option 3): The 2007 World Championships were held in Osaka, Japan, after India's first medal in 2003.

question: Tabla maestro, Bickram Ghosh, was awarded with which of the following awards in 2023 in the Contemporary Category?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tabla maestro Bickram Ghosh was conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2023 in the Contemporary/Innovative Music category, one of the highest official recognitions given by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, the national academy for music, dance and drama. (संगीत नाटक अकादमी पुरस्कार — बिक्रम घोष)

 

• Bickram Ghosh is a renowned tabla player, son of tabla legend Pandit Shankar Ghosh, known for blending Indian classical percussion with world/fusion music.

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) is conferred annually by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for the performing arts, recognising outstanding contributions to music, dance and drama.

 

• Award recipients also receive a Tamrapatra (bronze plaque), an angavastram, and a cash prize.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi was established in 1952 and is India's first National Academy of the Arts, functioning under the Ministry of Culture.

 

• Bickram Ghosh has composed music for several Bollywood and international projects and is known for pioneering the fusion genre in Indian percussion music.

 

NOTE

 

• Padma Shri (Option 1): A civilian award given by the Government of India; not the award referenced in this question for 2023.

 

• Padma Bhushan (Option 2): A higher civilian award; not the one awarded to Bickram Ghosh in this context.

 

• Sangeet Kalanidhi (Option 4): A prestigious title conferred by the Madras Music Academy for Carnatic music, unrelated to this award.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, the percentage of adolescent population (10-19 years) from the total population is how much?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 20.9%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the Census of India 2011, adolescents (10-19 years) constitute 20.9% of India's total population — roughly one-fifth of the country, amounting to about 253 million people. (किशोर जनसंख्या — कुल जनसंख्या का 20.9%)

 

• This large adolescent population is a key reason behind the Government of India's focus on adolescent health and development programmes.

 

• The Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK), launched in 2014 by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, specifically targets this age group, covering health concerns such as nutrition, mental health, substance misuse, and sexual/reproductive health.

 

• India has one of the largest adolescent populations in the world, making adolescent-focused policy a demographic priority.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The broader 'youth' population (15-29 years) as per Census 2011 constitutes about 27.5% of India's total population.

 

• The National Youth Policy and RKSK are among the key frameworks addressing India's large adolescent and youth demographic.

 

NOTE

 

• 22.9% (Option 1): Overstates the adolescent share of the population as per Census 2011.

 

• 21.9% (Option 2): Close to, but not the precise figure cited for the 10-19 age group as per Census 2011.

 

• 19.9% (Option 4): Understates the adolescent share of the population as per Census 2011.
